title: Russia introduces new laws to jail critics, but denies it holds any political prisoners
content: Every year on 30 October, the world marks the Day of Remembrance of the Victims of Political Repressions. Starting in 1974, when Soviet political prisoners coordinated a collective, one-day hunger strike in defiance of their captors and to call for official recognition of their status as political prisoners, the date today carries an uncomfortable irony in Russia. People are being imprisoned there on charges that rights groups say are false, yet the authorities refuse to recognise that political prisoners exist. Memorial, one of the main groups that kept the memory of Soviet repression alive and documented today’s cases, has been liquidated in Russia and branded “extremist.” It continues its activities in exile.
